releases.title: Build 2: hit sound also plays from file://
releases.author: game-developer
releases.body:
Assembled delivery: game-developer a08164312c18bd66f77ad40866fb05e1cdc3ff56 + artist sound/hit.wav 18f595a7f7373b331dd08c47c094d05136df8ed8.

**Start:** unzip `whack-a-mole-build-2.zip` and open `index.html` in Chromium, or run `python3 -m http.server 8000` in that folder and open http://localhost:8000/. Press Start.

Change from build 1: answers qa#4. Opened from file://, the hit sound now plays through an `<audio>` element. Before, it was silent and logged a fetch error. Over HTTP it still plays through Web Audio. Gameplay is unchanged.

Checked with `tools/check_round.py` on this assembled delivery in headless Chromium, both over HTTP and with `--file`: all checks pass. Round 30.0 s, every mole up < 1 s, no score from empty or repeated clicks, 17 hits = 17 points = 17 sounds, hit.wav 0.25 s, end screen and replay correct, console clean.

releases.title: Build 1: full playable round with hit sound
releases.author: game-developer
releases.body:
Assembled delivery: game-developer 130237e4f3b0225bc25d661f98ee81d5fc6034b9 + artist sound/hit.wav 18f595a7f7373b331dd08c47c094d05136df8ed8.

**Start:** unzip `whack-a-mole-build-1.zip`, run `python3 -m http.server 8000` in that folder, open http://localhost:8000/ in Chromium, press Start.

Checked with `tools/check_round.py` on this exact assembled delivery (headless Chromium): round 30.00 s; 34 moles, longest up 0.90 s (polled); empty-hole and repeated clicks never scored; 17 hits = 17 points = 17 sounds; decoded hit.wav 0.25 s; end screen shows final score; Play again resets to 0 / 30 s; no console errors.
